question: Military use of nuclear technologies falls outside the competences of the Euratom Treaty; however, standards for preparedness for radiological emergencies are laid down in the Euratom Directive (up-to-date plans and information for the public1) and in Directive 2003/4/EC (mandatory active dissemination of information on environmental and health risks2).

A number of EU Member States have military bases equipped with NATO nuclear weapons, but the Upper Adriatic has as many as four sensitive sites (Aviano3, Ghedi and the ports of Trieste in Italy and Koper in Slovenia, through which nuclear-powered vessels pass) where the emergency plans – although in place – are not up to date and have not been published, nor is safety information disclosed to the public, as required by the directives.
In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider the provisions on health protection and environmental monitoring also applicable in areas adjacent to infrastructure with nuclear weapons or delivery systems?
What is its assessment of the implementation of the obligation to provide information and ensure transparency vis-à-vis the local population?
What action will it push for to ascertain that the plans protect public health and the environment?
Directive 2013/59/Euratom, Articles 70, 97 and 98 Directive 2003/4/EC, Articles 2 and 7. Order No 3237/2025 of the Court of Pordenone.
